title: The append rule is stated as an invariant, not as a mechanism
head: ms-e30b9c47:d1
current_summary: The agent contract states the append INVARIANT - an entry is added at the physical end of its file, never inserted above existing content, and chronological order holds - and does not mandate the tool that achieves it. Shell append and Python append mode are optional tips, not requirements.
current_why: The contract is read by any file-reading agent, so mandating `>>` assumed shell or Python access and was platform-unsafe: the shell example simply fails for an agent that edits files directly. Stating the invariant lets each agent satisfy it with whatever writing surface it has, while the property that actually matters - nothing is inserted above existing content - is unchanged. This is distinct from Constitution Invariant #2, which says the past IS append-only; this concern is about how that rule is expressed to the agents bound by it.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Use `>>` / Python append mode as the required method for writing session entries. - R: Editor replace/insert requires an anchor line that may not be at the true end of the file if a prior edit added content after it. Append mode writes unconditionally to the physical end with no anchor, making correct ordering mechanical rather than reliant on care. - F: `.memory-seed/agent-rules.md`, `memory_seed/seed/.memory-seed/agent-rules.md`, both `session-log-check.py` copies, `core.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `tests/test_memory_seed.py`, all 13 seed `.md` frontmatter files. - T: 86 tests OK.

title: Derived never implicitly overrides write-time
head: mse_x1ha2e26md3q83zv:d1
current_summary: Sidecar precedence across families is source rank first, then recency. A `derived` block may never implicitly override a `write-time` block on the same subject - it may only fill a gap where no write-time value exists. An explicit override is possible but requires a human-reviewed `retracts:` naming the block it supersedes. Within a single source class most-recent-wins is unchanged. Provenance is recorded as first-hand versus reconstructed, not human versus machine.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "A `derived` block may **never** supersede a `write-time` block for the same subject" (mse_x1ha2e26md3q83zv:d1). Explicitly sets the precedence rule preventing derived blocks from overriding write-time values.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Sidecar precedence becomes `(source rank, then recency)` rather than recency alone. A `derived` block may **never** supersede a `write-time` block for the same subject; it may only fill a gap where no write-time value exists. Within a source class, most-recent-wins is unchanged. - R: Found while aligning the ADR contract — an agent flagged that once write-time values live in the sidecar, the existing most-recent-wins sort orders first-hand and reconstructed blocks *against each other*, so a sweep appending later would supersede the write-time value on recency alone. That directly contradicts Constitution v1.6, ratified hours earlier, which holds the two are **not equal evidence**. It is also already answered by JNL's stated intent — the sweep exists "for items which did not receive them at write time" — so a sweep able to overwrite a first-hand value would be a *source*, which the measured 0.583/0.613 reconstruction quality says it should not be. Leaving the hole open in an accepted proposal was the worse option: the read path is written against this rule. Useful side effect: it bounds the sweep's candidate set to subjects with no write-time value, which is what makes it cheap — it never re-judges what the write-time agent already answered. - A: Leave it as an open question for JNL — rejected: the answer follows from a ratified invariant plus an explicit instruction, and an accepted proposal with a hole in its precedence rule invites whoever builds step 1 to guess. Allow `derived` to win after human approval — not adopted, but flagged in the proposal as the one rule worth correcting before step 1, since a human-approved correction is the plausible case where recency *should* win. - F: `docs/2_Todo/write-time-sidecar-consolidation-proposal.md`, plus the ADR-alignment work merged from `claude/docs/adr-sidecar-provenance`. - T: `docs check` OK (180 files); `links check` OK (92 files). Docs-only.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: The rule now has two halves. (1) A `derived` block never **implicitly** supersedes a `write-time` block — precedence is `(source rank, then recency)`, so a sweep cannot win by being newer. (2) It may override one through an explicit `retracts:` naming it, **reviewed by a human before writing**. - R: My first draft stopped at half 1, which made write-time values permanently uncorrectable. JNL corrected it, and the correction is right: a write-time agent *can* be wrong, and a sweep reading the finished record sometimes has the better view, so freezing first-hand values would forfeit exactly the corrections worth having. What both halves together preserve is that a reconstructed value never displaces a first-hand one **silently** — it must state what it retracts, and a person must agree. This also reads Constitution v1.6 correctly: "not equal evidence" does not mean "reconstructed is never right", it means the burden sits on the reconstructed side — which is exactly what an explicit, reviewed retraction expresses. The human gate is not new machinery either; swarm output is already suggest-only and human-approved. - A: Keep half 1 alone (derived can only fill gaps) — rejected by JNL, and rightly: it optimises against one failure (silent override) by guaranteeing another (uncorrectable first-hand error). Allow implicit override once a human approves the sweep batch — rejected: approval of a batch is not approval of a specific displacement, and the read path could not tell the two apart. - F: `docs/2_Todo/write-time-sidecar-consolidation-proposal.md`, `docs/3_Spec/draft/sidecar-supersession-model.md`. - T: `docs check` OK (180 files); `links check` OK (92 files). Docs-only.

title: Docs taxonomy: folder is lifecycle state
head: mse_yfsrahvq87hxkcv9:d1
current_summary: Document lifecycle state is encoded in folder structure. Incoming material enters `docs/1_Inbox/`, active roadmap items sit in `docs/2_Todo/`, live normative specs occupy `docs/3_Spec/` (with candidates in `draft/`), source research lives in `docs/4_Reference/`, and terminal outcomes occupy `docs/5_Completed/`, `6_Rejected/`, `7_Replaced/`, or `8_Deferred/`.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "The FOLDER is now the single visible source of truth for a doc's lifecycle state" (mse_yfsrahvq87hxkcv9:d1). This decision made the folder itself the authoritative source for lifecycle state rather than using YAML fields.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Reworked the document-lifecycle plan to be folder-primary and human-discoverable. The FOLDER is now the single visible source of truth for a doc's lifecycle state (no `status:` field mirroring it); YAML carries only what a folder can't (priority, next_action, blocked_by, superseded_by/split_into, extracted_into, spec_binding); and a generated per-lane `README.md` index + a front-door roll-up is the human read surface (`memory-seed docs index`). Terminal/parked states are promoted to TOP-LEVEL lanes - `5_Completed`, `6_Rejected`, `7_Superseded`, `8_Deferred`; draft/candidate specs go to `3_Spec/draft/` and reference archive to `4_Reference/archived/`; blocked stays index-only inside `2_Todo`. `3_Spec` and `4_Reference` keep their numbers for path stability. `docs check` validates required-YAML-per-lane and pointer resolution (no folder-vs-status rule needed). Migration is phased: P1 small (create lanes + front door + move the 3 drifts + 2 draft specs), P2 bulk-move the 43 completed + update references. - R: User: a `rejected/` FOLDER makes it easier for a human to find live/applied vs dead work, and "the approach must be human discoverable too" - humans can't scan YAML tags. That flips my earlier machine-first design (status-field-as-truth) to folder-as-truth, which also deletes the status-vs-folder drift class entirely (the LANDED-in-Todo / PROPOSED-but-shipped drifts I'd found can't happen when the folder is the only state). User's three calls: draft subfolder, promote terminal states to top level, blocked index-only. - A: Chose folder = primary state + a generated index over more YAML, because a folder is human-visible and a file browser sorts it; kept multi-axis attributes (priority, blocked) in YAML+index since a folder is single-axis. Kept `3_Spec`/`4_Reference` numbers (renumbering would break dozens of path references - anti-discoverable). Blocked stays index-only (transient; a folder would churn on the flaky OneDrive `git mv`). Execution deferred; P1 is the small structural pass, pending approval. - F: docs/1_Inbox/document-lifecycle-system-plan.md - T: Docs only; no code or tests. `links check` green.

title: Hook installation is a per-agent merge, idempotent on script filename
head: ms-5e366ef4:d2
current_summary: Hook configuration is merged per agent rather than copied, across every supported agent's own config file. title: Link audit writes inert stubs; only an approval turns one into an edge
head: mse_63qcaab119xmyx0b:d2
current_summary: The link audit writes classified but INERT stubs for candidate lifecycle edges. A stub is never a live edge: it becomes one only through an explicit approval, and an entry whose candidates were all judged unrelated records that verdict rather than being left silently unexamined.
current_why: A sweep that wrote live edges directly would let a mechanical candidate generator author lineage, which is the one thing the edge grammar reserves for a deliberate act. Keeping the stub inert separates 'this pair might be related' from 'this pair IS related' - the first is cheap and can be wrong, the second is a claim the graph carries. Recording the negative verdict matters for the same reason: 'looked and found nothing' and 'never looked' are different states.

Grounded the answer - no background process: `link audit` is read-only by design, edges are hand-authored into `.memory-seed/sessions/links/YYYY-MM/*.md` and unioned at read time. The friction is that hand-authoring (path / frontmatter / yaml shape / chronology), the same drop-or-malform failure the entry-format lint just closed for entries. title: Append-only link retraction via retracts: blocks
head: mse_c3a4z35t4m4rjf1n:d1
current_summary: A published lifecycle edge is never edited in place. A downgrade or removal is expressed by appending a NEW sidecar block declaring `retracts: <kind> <ref> [(date)]`; the reader unions all edges then subtracts the retracted ones, and `links check` validates malformed, dangling and forward-only violations. A downgrade is a retract of the old kind plus a fresh edge of the new kind, authored together. `session merge-branch` refuses in-place edits to published link sidecars, and that guard is not to be bypassed.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "Added an append-only `retracts:` mechanism to link sidecars so a published lifecycle edge can be downgraded or removed" (mse_c3a4z35t4m4rjf1n:d1). Introduced the append-only retracts mechanism enabling non-destructive correction of published lifecycle edges.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Added an append-only `retracts:` mechanism to link sidecars so a published lifecycle edge can be downgraded or removed without reopening the block that declared it (which the fuse forbids). A new correction block declares `retracts: <kind> <ref> [(YYYY-MM-DD)]`; the reader (`entry_link_sidecars`) unions all edges then subtracts each retracted one (entry-level by `(kind, target)`, decision by the exact 4-tuple); `links check` validates malformed / dangling (nothing to retract) / forward-only (retract cannot pre-date the edge). A downgrade is a retract of the old kind plus a fresh edge of the new kind, authored together - so `evolves` becomes `related` with no block reopened. - R: The hand-audit exposed the gap directly: `session merge-branch` rightly refused my in-place edits to published sidecar blocks (append-only), and there was no sanctioned way to reclassify an edge, so I had to bypass the guard with a plain merge (JNL kept that correction but asked for a real mechanism). This closes it - future corrections use the path the fuse already accepts (a new block). Per JNL's steer, the retract identifies its target by kind + ref and is optionally pinned by the original declaration date ("use the date and the id"). - A: A `reclassifies:` one-liner (retract-plus-readd) was considered and deferred - the explicit retract+readd pair reads clearer. Editing blocks in place (rejected: bypasses the guard) and deleting them (rejected: destroys the evidence the edge existed) were the non-append-only alternatives. - F: memory_seed/core.py (parser, validator), memory_seed/retrieval.py (reader subtraction), tests/test_links_check.py (3 cases), docs/3_Spec/draft/link-retraction.md - T: 3 new retract tests pass; full backend suite; `links check` integrity OK

live_chain.body: - D: Converted the 5 hand-audit downgrades from in-place link-sidecar edits (an Invariant #2 violation) to append-only `retracts:` blocks: restored each original `evolves` edge and appended a `retracts: evolves <ref> (<date>)` + fresh `related_entries: <ref>` correction block, so the effective edge is still `related` but the history is append-only and the campaign's original claim is preserved. Also fixed a retract-reader bug the conversion exposed - an arrow-prefixed bare ref (`d2 -> X`) is collected as BOTH an entry-level edge and a source-only decision edge, so a retract must remove both twins or the decision one silently survives (pair mse_hejpp9whj0nn8jyy showed it). Added a regression test. - R: Reading `docs/CONSTITUTION.md` to update its durable facts surfaced that the earlier plain-merge of the in-place downgrades (`ea29bcc`) rewrote PUBLISHED link sidecars - exactly what Invariant #2 (append-only) forbids, and the v1.4 amendment log explicitly walls link sidecars off from in-place editing (citing the same fuse refusal I bypassed). At the time neither JNL nor I framed it as a constitutional violation and JNL said "keep it as is" - but that was before the sanctioned `retracts:` mechanism existed. Presented the finding; JNL chose to convert. This restores the corpus to Invariant #2 compliance and makes the pending docs honest. title: MCP integration: per-agent config placement, upsert semantics, and a gated write surface
head: mse_vzsef0fmpsde2jh4:d1
current_summary: Each agent's MCP config goes where that agent actually reads it - Claude in project-root `.mcp.json`, Codex in `.codex/config.toml` - written on init unconditionally rather than gated on a PATH probe. Merges upsert: a matching command is overwritten, a different one under the same key is left alone. The MCP write surface is gated, with `memory_session_append` the only authoring path, inheriting the same write-time guards as the CLI.
current_why: Config placement is per-agent because each vendor discovers servers differently, and writing to the wrong file fails silently. Upsert-on-matching-command protects a user's own server that happens to share our key while still keeping ours current. Unconditional write avoids a PATH probe that is wrong at init time anyway. The write surface is gated because an ungated pair let MCP writes bypass guards the CLI enforced - the write-surface parity rule.

live_chain.title: D1 - Write MCP config unconditionally, no PATH check at init time
live_chain.body: - D: `init_project` writes MCP server config for all three vendors unconditionally, without checking if `memory-seed-mcp` is on PATH first. - R: If the user ran `memory-seed init`, the binary shipped in the same package and should already be on PATH. Checking at init time adds complexity for a failure case that can't happen through normal persistent installation. - A: Check PATH at init and warn — rejected because the check is fragile (binary could disappear later) and doesn't cover the `uvx` case anyway. - F: `memory_seed/core.py`.

live_chain.title: D3 - MCP upsert: overwrite if command matches, skip if different command owns the key
live_chain.body: - D: MCP merge functions compare the full expected dict. If the key exists with a different `command`, leave it alone (user may have a different server named `memory-seed`). If the command matches but args differ, overwrite. - R: Protects user customization while still correcting stale args from our own prior installs. - F: `_merge_claude_mcp`, `_merge_cursor_mcp`, `_merge_gemini_mcp`.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Change `_MCP_SERVER_COMMAND` from `"memory-seed-mcp"` to `"uvx"` with `"memory-seed-mcp"` as the first arg. - R: Claude Code (and other agents) spawn MCP servers without inheriting the user's full PATH. `~/.local/bin` — where `uv tool` installs scripts — is not on Claude Code's PATH, so `memory-seed-mcp` was silently not found. `uvx` is part of uv and is typically available at the system level. - A: Hardcoding the absolute path was rejected — breaks portability across machines and users. - F: `memory_seed/core.py` (`_MCP_SERVER_COMMAND`, `_MCP_SERVER_ARGS`); `.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.gemini/settings.json` updated to match.

live_chain.title: D1 - Claude MCP server belongs in project-root .mcp.json, not settings.json
live_chain.body: - D: `_merge_claude_mcp` now writes `.mcp.json` at the project root (no `type` field); `.claude/settings.json` keeps hooks/permissions only. - R: Claude Code discovers project-scope MCP servers from `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add` - the `mcpServers` key in `settings.json` is the Cursor/generic format and is silently ignored. The bare {command,args} form (no type) was verified working in the issue report. - A: `claude mcp add` shell-out at init - rejected; fragile, needs the CLI on PATH and a live config, vs. a declarative checked-in file. - F: `memory_seed/core.py` (`_merge_claude_mcp`).

live_chain.title: D1 - Codex MCP belongs in project .codex/config.toml, written via zero-dep text upsert

head: ms-38098d7a:d1
current_summary: Per-user session files are written only when two or more participants are registered. A single configured user stays on the flat file, preserving the solo-first design. Reads discover both layouts, so the split is a write-time change rather than a migration, and an explicit `--user` bypasses the gate.

current_summary: The topic sidecar is the topic authority, not a derived overlay. Where an entry has sidecar attributions, those are its topics. Nothing authored is edited or deleted on disk; only which reading a consumer is shown changes, which is what keeps the switch reversible.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "`_topics()` now falls back in order: sidecar `inferred_topics`, then authored `topics:`, then the hashtag/heading axes." Only which of the two a READER is shown changed, and that is exactly what makes this reversible. - A: Union and mark provenance in the UI - rejected: it keeps the ambiguity and moves the cost to every consumer. title: Trace startup incremental; immutable git derivations persist
head: mse_gtn504wfjt3c34p6:d1
current_summary: Memory Trace startup is incremental: immutable git derivations (fork points, commit parents, changed paths) persist across rebuilds, reconciliation is incremental, and file-entry index is lazy.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "immutable git facts (a merge's fork point, a commit's parents, its first-parent changed paths) are computed once per commit EVER" (mse_gtn504wfjt3c34p6:d1). This decision established both architectural principles: persisting immutable git derivations and bulk-reading history in single passes.

live_chain.title: D1 - Persist immutable git derivations per sha; bulk-read history in single passes
live_chain.body: - D: Rebuilt the TraceCache enrichment pipeline around two principles: (1) immutable git facts (a merge's fork point, a commit's parents, its first-parent changed paths) are computed once per commit EVER and persisted in the disposable SQLite projection (schema v2: `fork_points`, `commit_parents`, `changed_paths`, `file_entries` tables), carried across full rebuilds; (2) all history harvesting happens in single delimited `git log` passes - fork points resolve in-process via maximal-common-ancestor over one bulk commit-graph read (with a `git merge-base` subprocess fallback only for criss-cross ambiguity), and per-work-commit changed paths come from one `git log --diff-merges=first-parent --name-only` pass instead of one `git diff` per commit. - R: Direct profiling on this corpus (new `python -m memory_trace.bench` harness, built FIRST per the task brief): full rebuild 44.3s spawning 990 git subprocesses, of which trailer/fork reconstruction was 17.4s/297 procs and the file-entry index 15.2s/342 procs - per-historical-item subprocess spawns at ~50-90ms each on Windows were the entire problem; parsing was 0.5s. The 2026-07-18 fork-point memo (entry `mse_81s84hmztx3ayqww`) fixed this within one process but was in-memory only, so every fresh server launch repaid the full walk. Retrieved the prior reasoning first: the projection contract (G1-G7) requires everything persisted to stay derived/rebuildable; unresolvable (None) fork points are deliberately NOT persisted so a deepened shallow clone can recover them. Body-scan trailer semantics (entry `mse_skpkqx0hhkw6ve4f`) and oldest-commit-wins attribution (entry `mse_e2vh8bqt4x0w6ljd`) preserved verbatim. - A: `_trunk_ref_and_sha`, `_commit_graph`, `_bulk_fork_points` (+ downward-closed-set maximality argument in its docstring), `_trailer_walk`/`_resolve_event_forks` (walk and fork resolution decoupled), `_changed_paths_bulk`, `_file_entry_index_from_parts` (pure derivation). Also fixed the pre-existing hardcoded-`main` asymmetry in `_file_entry_index` (now uses the main/master/HEAD fallback chain like its siblings). - T: Same corpus, same harness: full rebuild 44.3s/990 procs -> 1.46s/7 procs; trailer walk 17.4s -> 0.23s; file index 15.2s -> 0.78s. New regression test pins the count: rebuild subprocess total is IDENTICAL at 3 merges and 9 merges (per-item git work cannot silently return).

title: Trail derives display lanes without authored graph edges
head: mse_37fpco0vvunilz5k:d1
current_summary: Trail generates continuity lanes derived from lifecycle edges without requiring or adding authored graph edges.
current_why: Rests on the session decision that instituted it: "one straight lane per branch via interval coloring (lowest free lane, freed when the branch's visible life ends)" (mse_37fpco0vvunilz5k:d1). This decision rebuilt Trail as a git-graph timeline and established the algorithm for deriving lanes from branch intervals without authored graph edges.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Rebuilt Memory Trace's Trail view as a vertical git-graph timeline, replacing the shared force-layout graph engine it borrowed before. Newest entry on top; one straight lane per branch via interval coloring (lowest free lane, freed when the branch's visible life ends); lifecycle arcs bow through a left gutter - supersedes dashed red "replaces", evolves dotted blue "refines" (new `--edge-evolves` token #4f98d9); branch chip on each branch's tip row only; day separators; fixed 30px row height keeps the SVG rail index-aligned with HTML rows. Default window is the newest 60 entries with "Load older" (+60, client-side - the full corpus is fetched once). Server side: graph nodes now carry `branch` and `datetime`, `_graph_edges` emits `evolves`, and `_topics()` includes indexed `chunk.topics` - which also fixed the empty sidebar TOPICS facet and the topic filter in one line. Trail's fixed edge set is now branch+supersedes+evolves; plain relatedness dropped from Trail (it swamped the lineage signal). - R: User direction: "trail should be reminiscent of an interactive gitgraph timeline" + research brief consensus (GitKraken/Fork/Sublime Merge/VS Code Git Graph): vertical orientation, graph rail left + metadata right, straight lanes, bounded default window, dash+color dual encoding. User approved: recent window, minimal rows, chrome cuts, Space Grotesk+Inter. - A: Two research briefs (git-graph conventions; dense-UI de-crowding) were produced by sonnet subagents this session and synthesized into the four approved design decisions; remaining stages: de-crowding pass, typography pass. - F: `memory-trace/memory_trace/lense.py`, `memory-trace/memory_trace/static/app.js`, `memory-trace/memory_trace/static/styles.css`, `memory-trace/memory_trace/static/index.html`, `memory-trace/tests/test_lense.py`. - T: 38 memory-trace tests pass (2 new: evolves edges + node lineage fields; indexed-topics facets/filter). Live preview: 60 of 261 entries, 40 lane segments, 2 lifecycle arcs, branch tip chips, day separators; row click opens reader; Load older 60->120; console clean.

title: Trail: lifecycle visualization and decision-level row rendering
head: mse_zm2h343r4shfre3j:d2
current_summary: The Trail displays lifecycle edges (supersedes/evolves/related) between entries and decisions by default, ranked by precision into three classes: decision-to-decision and entry-to-decision edges drawn solid and bold, entry-to-entry edges drawn dashed and light. Multi-decision entries render one Trail row per decision, grouped under an anchor row, with edge selection scoped by entry so clicking any row in a group lights the entire entry's lineage.
current_why: The decision-level edges were recorded but invisible - every decision-level edge drew only on select, so the finest lineage links in the corpus were dark until clicked, and 189 entry-level evolves were equally hidden. Draw all three classes and let weight and opacity carry hierarchy, so history links read as quiet background rather than a wall. Decision rows must compute visibility and grouping by entry identity because selection state is entry-scoped, which is what stops a group from splitting.

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: Port the vanilla Trail to `/next` as a new `Trail` presentation mode. The layout math lives in a pure, framework-free `trailModel.ts` (a faithful port of `app.js:709-1008`): newest-first sort + day-separator rows, client-side windowing, branch spans, commit-time `interpRow`, fork/merge occupancy, greedy branch-lane interval packing (with the main-pinned-to-lane-0 guard and daisy-chain lane reuse), colour families, and merge events. `TrailWorkspace.tsx` renders the git-graph rail as JSX SVG (lane segments, solid+phantom main spine, rounded-elbow fork/merge connectors, clickable trunk merge dots) with day-grouped rows (time, title, branch pill) indented along the fork-to-merge silhouette; row/dot clicks select into the shared Inspector; a viewbar offers "Load older". Consumes `/api/v1/trail` (which already carries `branches`/`merges`/`continuity` — **pure frontend, no contract change**). - R: - Per the advisor's reframe, I built the **full model now** (lane packing + interpRow + fork/merge occupancy) rather than a Slice-2-only packing on entry spans, which would re-lane branches when the connector slice landed. And I shipped the **coherent cut = slices 1+2+3** (timeline + rail + connectors/merge dots): lanes-without-connectors is the *least* coherent stopping point — floating columns that promise a graph and hide the forks. Lifecycle arrows/brackets (Slice 4), continuity + search-dimming (Slice 5), and diagram badges (need `has_diagram` on the contract) are deferred; the relationship-lane zone is kept reserved so Slice 4 slots in without re-layout. - Trail correctness is the packing/interpRow algorithm, which the DOM cannot prove, so I exposed the built model as a `window.memoryTraceNextDebug` parity harness (mirroring the vanilla's intentional `memoryTraceDebug`) and asserted invariants on live 458-entry data: **main alone in lane 0**, every lane's intervals pairwise disjoint, laneCount 8 (not ~38), window respected (60 = min(60, total)), day separators present, all dots on integer lanes 0-7, DOM 108 circles = 60 node + 48 merge dots. - A: Rejected a flat "Trail" list (Slice 1 only) — it underdelivers when the user has seen the real git-graph. Rejected porting the bespoke Arc-2d **diagram** renderer here — it's ~250 lines and its own B0b remainder; the reader already shows a diagram count. - F: `memory-trace/client/src/trailModel.ts` (new), `TrailWorkspace.tsx` (new), `App.tsx`, `api.ts`, `styles.css`, rebuilt `memory_trace/static/react/*`, `docs/2_Todo/0_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. - T: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` clean; `test_static_serving.py` 9 pass; `docs check`/`docs index --check` current; live preview — model invariants all hold, row-click updates the Inspector, "Load older" 60→120, title/status/filter-bar coherent per mode, no console errors. **Bug caught in verification:** the `window` prop name shadowed the global `window`, so the parity-harness assignment threw in strict mode and blanked the app — renamed the prop to `windowSize`.

live_chain.title: D1 - Middle-third stability band with distance-eased scrolling
live_chain.body: - D: New `trailScroll.ts` owns Trail scroll movement. A selection whose row already sits in the middle third of the viewport does not move at all; one outside eases to that band's **near** edge (top when above, bottom when below) over an `easeInOutCubic` whose duration scales with distance (180-600ms), cancelling any in-flight run. `prefers-reduced-motion` jumps instantly. - R: JNL asked for stability between neighbouring selections and directional, accelerating travel otherwise. Native `scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"})` can target neither a specific band edge nor scale its duration, so a small rAF pass is the honest implementation rather than gold-plating. Row geometry comes from the model (`index * TRAIL_ROW + TRAIL_ROW/2`), not DOM measurement, since the rail already shares those coordinates. - A: Rejected `block:"center"`: recentring is what JNL called "very annoying" earlier, and it moves the list even when the row is already comfortably in view. - F: `trailScroll.ts` (new), `TrailWorkspace.tsx`. - T: `trailScroll.test.ts` (10 cases: band hold, both edges, direction, clamping, no-op at the extremes, duration bounds, easing symmetry). In-browser: landed on **exactly** 266px (top edge) and 533px (bottom edge) of an 799px viewport, held still when in-band, 27 eased frames per journey.

Only a deliberate selection should move the list. - F: `TrailWorkspace.tsx`. - T: verified `scrollTop == 0` on reload with a selection already present.

live_chain.title: D1 - Surface decisions as Trail rows via the section chunks that already carry their identity
live_chain.body: - D: Multi-decision entries (>=2 `#### Dn -` decisions) now render one Trail row per decision, at JNL's request: D1 is the entry's existing row (entry time, full branch colour); D2..DN are additional rows on the same branch lane with a pastel of the branch colour and a bracket right of the time column grouping the set. Implemented as a Trail-only backend opt-in (`TraceService.graph(include_decisions=True)`, passed solely by `/api/v1/trail`): the expansion reads the section-granularity chunks already materialised per `#### Dn` heading - whose chunk_id `{entry_id}#decisions/dN-<slug>` IS the ratified decision identity `(entry_id, dN)` from the ADR contract amendment (`mse_v9stt3nxkg7s4m84`) - so no new identity scheme, no new parsing, one memoized SQL read, zero git work (the incremental-startup guarantees stay intact). - R: Retrieved the prior reasoning first: the ADR contract had already settled decision identity as the `(entry_id, ordinal)` pair with the section slug as the retrieval address, and `_find_section_ranges` already splits entries at `###`+ headings - the Trail was the only surface not exposing it. Detection reuses core's write-time-validated grammar via a newly exported `DECISION_TITLE_ORDINAL_RE` (bare-title form of `_NUMBERED_DECISION_HEADING_RE`) so Trail detection can never drift from what `session append` accepts. Singular-`### Decision` entries (the 346-entry majority) deliberately keep `decision_ordinal: None` rather than the ADR "d1 by convention" reading - that convention is identity semantics, not rendering; None doubles as the client's "not part of a rendered group" flag and guarantees zero change for existing entries. Child rows strip continuity and diagram badges (entry-scoped affordances would misread as N events); lifecycle edges/merges/branches compute before expansion, staying entry-scoped by construction (decision-specific EDGES await the sidecar contract's implementation). - A: Considered full section granularity through `graph()` instead - rejected: the trail needs only decision sections, and granularity="all" has been deliberately dead since the projection shipped. - F: `memory_seed/core.py` (regex export), `memory-trace/memory_trace/models.py` (GraphNode `decision_ordinal`/`decision_count`), `memory-trace/memory_trace/service.py` (`_expand_decision_rows`, `include_decisions`), regenerated `memory-trace/tests/contract/{openapi.v1.json,types.ts}` per the documented workflow, `memory-trace/tests/test_trail_decision_rows.py` (new, 5 tests), `memory-trace/tests/test_v1_api_contract.py` (hardened: first-row-per-entry wins, the last-wins dict would silently compare a child's empty continuity).

live_chain.title: D1 - Decision
live_chain.body: - D: A multi-decision entry's Trail rows are now a HEADING plus SUBHEADINGS: the entry row is the group anchor (`decision_ordinal=None`, `decision_count=N`, full branch colour, keeps the timestamp) and EVERY decision D1..DN gets its own pastel row. Previously the entry row doubled as D1, so the Trail went entry title -> D2 -> D3 with no D1 anywhere. - R: JNL: "D1 should be seperately visible too as the multidecisions should act as subheadings - it makes no sense to skip heading 1." Right on both counts. Conflating the entry title with D1 also conflated two different strings - the entry title names the WORK, D1 names a decision inside it - so the D1 heading text was simply never displayed. Uniform pastel for D1..DN is what makes the heading/subheading reading legible; the anchor keeps full colour because it is the event, and the decisions are structure inside it. - A: The mechanical core was that `decision_ordinal === "d1"` had been the codeword for "this is the anchor" at six sites. After this change absent-ordinal means anchor and "d1" is an ordinary child, so every one of those sites inverts. Rather than flip them individually I exported two predicates from `trailModel.ts` - `isDecisionRow` (styling: pastel dot, indent, no timestamp) and `inDecisionGroup` (grouping: shared indent block, group search highlight, exact-chunk selection) - which differ EXACTLY on the anchor. That distinction is the whole feature, and naming it stops the next edit from collapsing the two again. Three traps the "tests pass" signal would not have caught, all found by reasoning through the anchor's new dual status before editing: (1) the bracket tooltip counted rows, and the span now includes the anchor, so it would have claimed N+1 decisions - it reads `decision_count` now; (2) `isSelected`'s permissive entry_id match would have lit the anchor ALONGSIDE whichever decision was selected, since the anchor also carries the group's entry_id - it is gated on `inDecisionGroup` so exactly one row lights in both states; (3) the indent-stabilising group scan keyed on `decision_ordinal`, so with the anchor's ordinal gone the group would have started at D1 and left the heading out of the block indent - reintroducing the exact stagger the previous session's fix closed. Fixed a latent bug for free: a full-text hit inside a D1 section set a `#decisions/d1-` chunk hint, but no row carried that chunk_id, so the highlight silently landed nowhere. Verified against the live corpus - the three D1 sections search returns all now resolve to real rows. - F: `memory-trace/memory_trace/service.py` (`_expand_decision_rows`), `memory-trace/client/src/trailModel.ts` (predicates, entry-honest total, group-safe window), `TrailWorkspace.tsx`, `App.tsx` (Recent list filter), `tests/test_trail_decision_rows.py`, `client/src/trailModel.test.ts`, rebuilt `memory_trace/static/react/`. No contract regen: both fields already exist, only their meaning changed. - T: 82 client unit tests (1 new predicate test), 7 axe a11y, 5 Playwright e2e, 178 memory-trace backend tests, typecheck and production build all pass. Live-verified against the real corpus: trail nodes 717 -> 823 (+106, exactly one new D1 row per group); the 19:25 entry renders 4 rows (heading + D1 + D2 + D3) at an identical 213px indent with the time on the anchor only; clicking each of the four lights exactly one row; bracket tooltips read 3 decisions for 4-row groups and 2 for 3-row groups; the Recent list still shows 24 unique entries with no decision titles leaking and no duplicates; "45 of 542 entries" stays entry-honest.

live_chain.title: D2 - The Trail draws all lifecycle edges by default, weighted by a three-class granularity model
live_chain.body: - D: The default view draws every lifecycle edge, ranked by precision: decision->decision (class 1) and entry<->decision (class 2) solid and bold; entry->entry (class 3) dashed and light. An entry can evolve another entry, so class-3 history links and the swarm-era edges are real lineage and stay visible, not hidden. A three-state setting (On select / Decision / All) keeps the de-crowded views available; All is default. - R: The grammar-v2 edges were recorded but unusable - every decision-level edge is an `evolves`, and evolves drew only on select, so the finest links in the corpus were dark until clicked. Fixing that first surfaced that entry-level evolves (189 of them, including the 66 swarm-era) were equally hidden. JNL's call: draw all three classes, let weight and opacity carry the hierarchy so a screen of history links reads as quiet background rather than a wall. - A: Keep decision-only as the default (my first cut) - rejected by JNL: entry->entry is legitimate and should show. Draw everything at equal weight - rejected: 211 arcs at full ink is the wall the class weighting exists to avoid. - F: `memory-trace/client/src/trailModel.ts` (`lifecycleEdgeClass`), `TrailWorkspace.tsx`, `SettingsMenu.tsx`, `App.tsx`. - T: `trailModel.test.ts` covers the classifier; verified live with the full corpus loaded - 181 arcs + 31 bracket chains, weights stepping 2.8/2.6/2.5, class 3 at 0.5 opacity. 138 client tests pass.
